source.title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures

accepted.question_text: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two, where “non-special” means that P is neither a Lattès map nor conjugate to z^±n or ±T_n for some n ≥ 2. Let C(P) be the semigroup of rational functions commuting with P, and let G_P be the finite quotient group obtained from C(P) by identifying Q_1 and Q_2 whenever Q_1∘P^{∘l_1} = Q_2∘P^{∘l_2} for some l_1, l_2 ≥ 0. Which finite groups can occur as G_P?

evidence.quote: We will call a rational function special if it is either a Latt`es map or it is conjugate to z^±n, n ≥ 2, or ±T_n, n ≥ 2, where T_n is the nth Chebyshev polynomial.
Theorem 2.2. Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then the relation ~_P is a congruence on the semigroup C(P), and the quotient semigroup is a finite group.
Problem 2.3. Which finite groups occur as groups G_P for non-special rational functions P?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Associate to P the finite multigraph Γ_P whose vertices represent chosen conjugacy-class representatives inside the equivalence class of P under elementary transformations P = V∘U, P' = U∘V, and whose edges correspond to decompositions linking such representatives. Which finite graphs can occur as Γ_P?

evidence.quote: The graph Γ_P is defined as a multigraph whose vertices are in a one-to-one correspondence with some fixed representatives P_i of conjugacy classes in [P], and whose multiple edges connecting the vertices corresponding to P_i to P_j are in a one-to-one correspondence with solutions of the system P_i = V ∘ U, P_j = U ∘ V in rational functions.
Problem 2.4. Which finite graphs occur as graphs Γ_P for non-special rational functions P?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Define C_∞(P) = ⋃_{k≥1} C(P^{∘k}), where C(P^{∘k}) is the semigroup of rational functions commuting with the k-th iterate of P. Is it true that there exist finitely many rational functions X_1, …, X_r such that a rational function X belongs to C_∞(P) if and only if X = X_j∘P^{∘k} for some j with 1 ≤ j ≤ r and some k ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Let us define the sets C∞(P) and Aut∞(P) by the formulas C∞(P) = ⋃∞_{i=1} C(P^{∘k}), Aut∞(P) = ⋃∞_{k=1} Aut(P^{∘k}).

Conjecture 3.1. Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then there exist finitely many rational functions X1, X2, . . . , Xr such that a rational function X belongs to C∞(P) if and only if X = Xj ∘ P^{∘k} for some j, 1 ≤ j ≤ r, and k ≥ 0.

accepted.question_text: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Is there an integer s ≥ 1 such that the semigroup C_∞(P), defined as the union of the commuting semigroups C(P^{∘k}) over all k ≥ 1, is exactly equal to C(P^{∘s})?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then C∞(P) = C(P^{∘s}) for some s ≥ 1.

accepted.question_text: Call a rational function A of degree at least two tame if the algebraic curve (A(x) − A(y)) / (x − y) = 0 has no irreducible factors of genus 0 or 1, and call A wild otherwise. Describe all wild rational functions.

evidence.quote: Let A be a rational function of degree at least two. We say that A is tame if the algebraic curve (8) A(x) − A(y) / (x − y) = 0 has no factors of genus zero or one. Otherwise, we say that A is wild.
Problem 3.4. Describe wild rational functions.

accepted.question_text: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two, and let E(P) be the semigroup consisting of rational functions Q of degree at least two that share the measure of maximal entropy μ_P with P, together with the μ_P-invariant Möbius transformations. Is it true that there exist finitely many rational functions X_1, …, X_r such that X belongs to E(P) if and only if X = X_j∘P^{∘k} for some j with 1 ≤ j ≤ r and some k ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: For a rational function P of degree at least two, we denote by μ_P the measure of maximal entropy for P, and by E(P) the set of rational functions Q of degree at least two such that μ_Q = μ_P, completed by μ_P-invariant Möbius transformations. The set E(P) is a semigroup.

Conjecture 3.5. Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then there exist finitely many rational functions X1, X2, . . . , Xr such that X belongs to E(P) if and only if X = Xj ∘ P^{∘k} for some j, 1 ≤ j ≤ r, and k ≥ 0.

accepted.question_text: Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two. Suppose that for every n, m ≥ 1, the algebraic curve A^{∘n}(x) − B^{∘m}(y) = 0 has a factor of genus 0 or 1. Must it follow that either both A and B are special (that is, Lattès maps or maps conjugate to z^±n or ±T_n for some n ≥ 2), or else A and B have a common iterate, meaning that A^{∘k} = B^{∘l} for some k, l ≥ 1?

evidence.quote: We will call a rational function special if it is either a Latt`es map or it is conjugate to z^±n, n ≥ 2, or ±T_n, n ≥ 2, where T_n is the nth Chebyshev polynomial.

Conjecture 4.2. Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two such that all algebraic curves (12) have a factor of genus zero or one. Then either both A and B are special or there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that A^{∘k} = B^{∘l}.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two that contains at least one non-special function. Is S left reversible if and only if any two elements of S have a common iterate? Here left reversible means that for every A, B in S there exist X, Y in S such that A∘X = B∘Y.

evidence.quote: We recall that a semigroup S is called left reversible if for all A, B in S there exist X, Y in S such that (1) AX = BY.

Conjecture 4.3. Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special function. Then S is left reversible if and only if any two elements of S have a common iterate.

accepted.question_text: Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two. If some forward orbit of A has infinite intersection with some forward orbit of B, must A and B have a common iterate?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two such that an orbit of A has an infinite intersection with an orbit of B. Then A and B have a common iterate.

accepted.question_text: Given rational functions A and B of degree at least two, under what conditions does the intersection of the function fields C(A) and C(B) contain a non-constant rational function?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.5. Given rational functions A and B of degree at least two, under what conditions does the field C(A) ∩ C(B) contain a non-constant rational function?

accepted.question_text: Let A be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Do there exist rational functions X and F, with X a Galois covering and X∘A = F∘X, such that for every rational function B of degree at least two the following are equivalent: (i) for every n ≥ 1, the field C(A^{∘n}) ∩ C(B) contains a non-constant rational function, and (ii) B is a compositional right factor of X∘A^{∘ℓ} for some ℓ ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.6. Let A be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then there exist rational functions X and F such that X is a Galois covering, the diagram (14) ... commutes, and for a rational function B of degree at least two all fields (13) contain a non-constant rational function if and only if B is a compositional right factor of X ∘ A^{∘ℓ} for some l ≥ 0.

accepted.question_text: Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two such that for every n ≥ 1 the field C(A^{∘n}) ∩ C(B) contains a non-constant rational function. Must it follow that either both A and B are special, or else there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k}∘B^{∘l} and B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l}∘A^{∘k}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.7. Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two such that all fields (13) contain a non-constant rational function. Then either both A and B are special or there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that the equalities A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k} ∘ B^{∘l}, B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l} ∘ A^{∘k} hold.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special function. Is S right reversible if and only if for every pair A, B in S there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k}∘B^{∘l} and B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l}∘A^{∘k}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.8. Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special function. Then S is right reversible if and only if for any two elements A, B of S there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that the equalities A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k} ∘ B^{∘l}, B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l} ∘ A^{∘k} hold.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Are the following conditions equivalent: (1) S is amenable; (2) S is left amenable; (3) S is left reversible; (4) any two elements of S have a common iterate; and (5) S is a subsemigroup of C_∞(P) for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Then the following conditions are equivalent. 1) The semigroup S is amenable. 2) The semigroup S is left amenable. 3) The semigroup S is left reversible. 4) Any two elements of S have a common iterate. 5) The semigroup S is a subsemigroup of C∞(P) for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Are the following conditions equivalent: (1) S is right amenable; (2) S is right reversible; (3) for every A, B in S there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k}∘B^{∘l} and B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l}∘A^{∘k}; (4) S contains no free subsemigroup of rank two; and (5) S is a subsemigroup of E(P) for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.2. Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special rational function. Then the following conditions are equivalent. 1) The semigroup S is right amenable. 2) The semigroup S is right reversible. 3) For any two elements A, B of S there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that the equalities A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k} ∘ B^{∘l}, B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l} ∘ A^{∘k} hold. 4) The semigroup S contains no free subsemigroup of rank two. 5) The semigroup S is a subsemigroup of E(P) for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two.
